node_definition.done_when:
Three parts, all in the unresolvable-commit region of reckon/crew/promotion.py on your base, which is current main.

Part one ports run r-20261001T051714453460-one-refusal-lists-every-precondition. Its commits are 5bfd82b52c98bf09bedda6ea6c00922df1b082af and e0434c29b88a58ce92e54fbc53deadb9722d1f47; read them with git show. They no longer merge, because main's complete() changed in the same region at ee3f37084 and b4233a9cb. Re-implement them on your base:
- crew complete reports every independently judgeable precondition in one refusal, with the first one's wording first;
- the stored-review refusal names the reviewed head to cite;
- cited revisions are canonicalised through _resolve_commits, so the ledger row records full shas;
- main's reconcile behaviour stays intact.

Part two fixes a regression on main that started when a399d7744 made the presented branch refuse unresolvable values. A review run whose commits field is a commitless declaration in prose (for example: none, review node, no repository change, the review is the deliverable) is now refused as an unresolvable presented commit. A commitless declaration that the existing declaration parser recognises means no commits. A word that only begins with an absence word is still not a declaration.

Part three gives one vocabulary to every unresolvable-commit refusal: presented, declared and resolver. Today tests/test_crew.py::test_promotion_refuses_a_commit_that_names_no_object expects 'does not resolve to a commit object', and tests/test_commitless_review_promotes.py expects 'does not resolve to an object'. Choose one, and update whichever test pins the superseded wording, giving the reason in the commit message.

Before changing anything, record the base arm at current main: tests/test_commitless_review_promotes.py has 4 failures (test_a_report_only_review_promotes_over_its_own_deliverable, test_a_review_with_commits_prose_promotes_on_a_clean_worktree, test_an_implement_run_whose_commits_do_not_resolve_is_refused, test_a_word_that_only_begins_with_an_absence_word_is_not_a_declaration).

At head, those four pass, along with:
- tests/test_crew.py::test_promotion_refuses_a_commit_that_names_no_object;
- tests/test_cited_identifier_resolves.py;
- tests/test_one_refusal_on_main.py, which carries over the cases of tests/test_one_refusal_lists_every_precondition.py from e0434c29b, adapted to main;
- tests/test_control_gate_repairs.py, tests/test_a_short_commit_list_is_reported.py and tests/test_gate_evidence.py.

Execute two named controls and record each log: with the aggregation reverted, the two-precondition case fails; with the commitless-declaration check removed from the presented branch, the report-only review case fails.

Evidence rules:
- Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder.
- Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code.
- Every pytest process uses a basetemp private to that process.
- ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not.
- Do not run a whole-population sweep; the coordinator measures the population after merge.

Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. An evidence fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/scoring-should-stop-a-promotion/one-refusal-on-main.html records the port, the regression fix and the chosen vocabulary. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
